**Finding: compliant (no redline).**

Section 13.4.1 is a mutual assignment clause that already contains the carve-out we look for: either Party — including AbbVie — may assign without the other's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor by merger, sale of stock or sale of assets of the relevant business, and any other assignment requires consent that may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. That meets (indeed exceeds) the fallback position and is far from the walk-away.

On change of control, the mechanics in Section 13.2 run **against Harpoon only** (notice of a Harpoon Change in Control or Acquisition, with consequences under 13.2.2), reinforced by our Competitor-triggered rights in Sections 2 and 5. Harpoon has no termination or re-pricing right on an AbbVie change of control, so there is nothing to delete.

Noted for the record but not flagged (preferred-only refinements): the clause does not prohibit Harpoon from assigning to an AbbVie competitor, and the consent restriction is mutual rather than one-way in our favour.
